propositions: The documented curl command targeting `$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)` resolves to the shared hook directory when run from a linked worktree, silently overwriting the pre-commit wrapper in the main checkout rather than affecting only the current worktree.

The curl-based installation destroys the pre-commit wrapper chain, causing the Gerrit Change-Id stamper and pre-commit message validation to both stop running, with failures only surfacing at push time in potentially different worktrees.

The idempotent `make hooks` target and new `scripts/install-gerrit-hook.sh` script install the Gerrit hook to `commit-msg.legacy` when a pre-commit wrapper exists, preserving both the wrapper and the Change-Id logic in the migration chain.

AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md documentation must remove instructions to curl directly to `--git-path hooks/commit-msg` and instead direct users to `make hooks` as the single documented installation path.

The installer script must refuse to overwrite a non-wrapper, non-stamper commit-msg hook and validate that fetched payloads contain Change-Id logic before installation, making unsafe overwrites loud rather than silent.
